posts.text: 2w The clock for a review request starts at the door. A checkout date tells you when money changed hands. It does not tell you whether a customer has received the product, let alone experienced it. When a review request fires while the parcel is still in transit, you are not collecting product feedback. You are inviting delivery frustration into a retention moment. Use two conditions: → confirmed delivery → enough time to use the product The second condition changes by category. For many physical goods, 7 to 14 days after confirmed delivery is a reasonable starting point. Then stop the sequence once the customer responds. Trigger off the event. Not the schedule.
